findings.issue_text: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py (~line 254), the restart path can never kill a hung flusher process: processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process (SpawnProcess), which is a sibling class of multiprocessing.Process rather than a subclass, so the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check is always False and kill() is never invoked. Each hang event leaks a wedged process that still holds a popped segment and can resume and race with its replacement over the same Redis shards (duplicate segment production to Kafka); the except (ValueError, AttributeError) clause and the terminate() backstop in join() are likewise dead code. This is a regression from the pre-PR code that called kill() unconditionally; fix by checking against SpawnProcess (or BaseProcess) and killing before spawning the replacement.

In flusher.py _create_process_for_shards (~lines 100-128), thread-mode hang restart silently duplicates flusher workers: in produce_to_pipe mode a hung threading.Thread cannot be killed and has no per-thread stop signal, so on a hang a second thread is spawned for the same shards while the first keeps running, causing two threads to poll and produce the same segments concurrently (duplicated output in the pipe). The old code failed loudly here (Thread.kill raised an uncaught AttributeError); the new code fails silently.

In flusher.py (~lines 45, 54), the unvalidated flusher_processes/max_processes value produces degenerate topologies with all self-protection disabled: --flusher-processes=0 is swallowed by the `or` and silently becomes one-process-per-shard, and a negative value yields min(-1, n) = -1 so range(-1) is empty and zero flusher processes are created. With empty processes/buffers, submit()'s guards are all vacuous (no backpressure rejection can ever fire and the Redis-memory check is skipped), so the consumer keeps buffering into Redis unboundedly while reporting healthy. click.Option(type=int) accepts these values.

In flusher.py (~line 202), the metric tag key mismatch fragments the flusher metrics: wait_produce is tagged {"shards": shard_tag} while produce and segment_size_bytes use {"shard": shard_tag}, so the same dimension lives under two tag keys and any dashboard/alert slicing spans.buffer.flusher.* by shard silently misses the wait_produce series.

In tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py (~lines 62-65), the added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op: the test opens by monkeypatching time.sleep globally to a no-op lambda, so the intended wait to give flusher threads time to process after a drift change never happens and the test's actual stability rests on the flusher threads busy-spinning. The misleading comment could cause the test to break for the wrong reason if the monkeypatch is ever scoped.

In flusher.py join (~lines 334-345), the expired-deadline break abandons the remaining processes: waiting is sequential per process, so if the first (wedged) process consumes the whole deadline, the break skips both the wait and the terminate() for every remaining flusher process, losing the shutdown backstop for all but the first hung process (bounded impact since remaining processes observe the shared stopped flag and are daemons).

In factory.py:41 / flusher.py:47, the new flusher_processes/max_processes parameters were inserted mid-signature before produce_to_pipe: any positional caller passing the pipe callable as the next argument now binds it to flusher_processes, producing min(<callable>, len(...)) and a TypeError at construction, or for SpanFlusher a silently-None produce_to_pipe so produced payloads go nowhere. All in-diff callers use keywords, but out-of-diff positional callers are affected; the new params should be appended at the end instead.

`flusher_processes` is unvalidated in flusher.py:51/60-66: a falsy `0` from `--flusher-processes 0` is silently swallowed by `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and becomes one process per assigned shard (a silent resource explosion of spawn-context interpreters, Redis pools, and Kafka producers contradicting the option's help text), while negative values pass through `min()` as negative, making `range(num_processes)` empty so `self.process_to_shards_map[0]` raises KeyError at :65-66 and crash-loops the consumer; needs `max(1, ...)` or explicit bounds validation.

N+1 Redis round-trips per submitted batch in `submit()` (flusher.py:269-270 and :300-302): new code loops over `self.buffers.values()` — one buffer per flusher process — issuing N sequential Redis round trips for the exact same total key set that a single all-shards buffer could have covered in one pipelined call, so per-batch ingestion latency grows linearly with process count whenever `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage < 1.0`.

Hung flusher threads can't be killed but a replacement is spawned anyway (flusher.py:~246-256, `_ensure_processes_alive`): the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard means the threading (`produce_to_pipe`) mode never kills the unhealthy thread, yet `_create_process_for_shards()` immediately starts a second thread for the same shards — the hung thread leaks permanently, risks duplicate produce if it later un-hangs, and health monitoring only watches the replacement, making the zombie invisible; the old code at least failed loudly via `Thread.kill()` AttributeError.

Metric volume and cardinality multiplied by process count plus a tag-key inconsistency (flusher.py:~185-196, ~231-235, ~278-280): each of N processes emits `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `.wait_produce`, and `segment_size_bytes` per flush cycle tagged with a joined shard list that churns on every Kafka rebalance (unbounded distinct series), and `wait_produce` uses tag key "shards" while its siblings use "shard", splitting one logical metric into duplicate series.

`get_memory_info` summed across per-process buffers can double-count Redis services and skew the backpressure ratio (flusher.py:~300-303): if a Redis service hosts shards assigned to multiple processes under round-robin distribution, its stats are counted once per buffer instead of deduped as the old single all-shards buffer did, so the `used/available` ratio differs from the true cluster ratio and `max-memory-percentage` trips at the wrong point — over-rejecting messages or under-protecting Redis from OOM.

`join()` skips `terminate()` for all remaining processes once the shared deadline expires (flusher.py:~330-346): if the deadline expires while waiting on an early process, `break` exits the for-loop and every later child is never terminated, the first slow process consumes the entire timeout budget leaving the rest zero grace, and in the window before parent exit the un-terminated children keep polling Redis and can produce to Kafka after the pipeline has closed.

The new test wait is a no-op and the race it was added to fix remains (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:~60-62): the added `time.sleep(0.1)` runs after `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` patches the global `time` module, so the test's own call is also a no-op and no time is actually yielded — if `step.join()` sets `stopped` before the flusher thread observes the drift change and produces, the segment is never flushed and assertions can fail intermittently; use a wait that bypasses the patch or restore it before sleeping.

Spawn-mode entrypoint `SpanFlusher._main_process` was not updated for the new required `shards` parameter added to `main()`, so the multiprocessing target receives 7 positional args against a 6-parameter signature and crashes with a TypeError the moment each production flusher child process boots, causing a consumer crash loop after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS; CI won't catch it because tests pass `produce_to_pipe` and take the threading path.

No validation on the `flusher_processes` CLI option: `--flusher-processes 0` silently spawns one process per shard (behavior inversion from `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)`), and negative values build an empty `process_to_shards_map` leading to a KeyError crash loop in `create_with_partitions`; needs `click.IntRange(min=1)` or an assert in `__init__`.

Long, high-cardinality shard-list tags (comma-joined list of all shards a process handles, e.g. '0,1,…,63' in the default config) are re-emitted on hot-path timers (`produce`, `segment_size_bytes`, `wait_produce`) every flush cycle, and the set of distinct tag values grows with every partition rebalance across the fleet, burdening the metrics pipeline.

`flusher_unhealthy` now fans out per shard, so a single unhealthy process emits one increment per shard, making alert counts scale with shards-per-process (a single restart looks up to N× worse) and losing comparability with pre-PR dashboards.

Inconsistent metric tag key: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": ...}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": ...}`, so timers describing the same flush cycle cannot be sliced/joined on a common dimension — almost certainly a typo.

Dead helper `_create_process_for_shard` has no call sites and is a latent duplicate-flusher footgun: if ever wired up, it would start a second process for the shard group without killing the old one and without incrementing `process_restarts`, bypassing the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS safety and producing duplicate concurrent flushers/duplicate Kafka production; remove it or route it through the kill/restart path.

The `time.sleep(0.1)` added to `test_basic` is a no-op because the test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` globally, so the claimed 'give flusher threads time to process after drift change' synchronization doesn't exist and the test still relies on a race between the flusher thread reading `current_drift` and `step.join()`, remaining theoretically flaky.

Health check still only runs from `submit()`: `poll()` (invoked every arroyo loop iteration, even with no messages) only forwards to `next_step` and never invokes `_ensure_processes_alive()`, so an idle consumer never detects or restarts a dead flusher process until a message arrives, allowing Redis-buffered segments to age out past TTL and be lost.

The new multiprocess test test_flusher_processes_limit verifies only internal wiring, never data flow: it submits no spans, never asserts messages or commits, and never inspects flusher.buffers[i] to confirm each per-process SpansBuffer was built from the correct shard subset, so a regression that passes the full shard list to every process (duplicate Kafka production of spans) or drops a shard from buffer construction (silent span loss) would pass undetected; the shard-total assertion (total_shards == 4) also cannot catch mis-assignment since a duplicated shard plus a dropped shard still sums to 4.

The rewritten health-monitoring/restart logic in _ensure_processes_alive (per-process process_healthy_since dict, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS → RuntimeError, per-shard unhealthy metric fan-out, and the new isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)-guarded kill path) has zero test coverage; notably the isinstance guard is a behavior change — previously a thread-mode restart raised an uncaught AttributeError on Thread.kill(), whereas now the old (possibly hung) thread is silently left running while a new thread is started for the same shards — and nothing pins this new behavior.

The synchronization sleep added to test_basic is a no-op: the test monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op at its top, so the later time.sleep(0.1) intended to give flusher threads time to process after the drift change does literally nothing — either the author was ineffectively papering over a real race (drift change → flush ordering across threads) whose flake remains latent, or the line is dead code misleading future maintainers about how the test works.

The --flusher-processes click option is bare type=int with no bounds and the flusher performs no validation: flusher_processes=-1 yields max_processes = -1, an empty process_to_shards_map, and a KeyError in SpanFlusher.__init__ that crash-loops the consumer at startup; flusher_processes=0 silently falls through the 'or' to one-process-per-shard, contradicting the documented 'Defaults to 1' semantics; and no test covers 0, negative values, or the actual production default topology (1 process with many shards).

Metric tag key mismatch in the new health metrics: wait_produce is tagged with tags={'shards': shard_tag} while produce and segment_size_bytes use tags={'shard': shard_tag}, so the wait-time series won't group with its sibling metrics in dashboards/alerts, and no test asserts the emitted tags, which is why the mismatch slipped through.

Backpressure test coverage was weakened to an any() assertion (any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())) that only confirms at least one process noticed backpressure — a bug where some processes never record backpressure would still pass — and the new per-process gating semantics in submit() (raising MessageRejected when any single process exceeds the threshold, plus the per-process flusher.backpressure metric emission) have no coverage at all.

Multi-process join(timeout) budget-sharing behavior changed and is untested: with multiple processes the first slow process can consume the entire timeout, and once remaining_time <= 0 the break skips both waiting and terminate() for all remaining processes (daemon=True masks the leak, but graceful drain is skipped and in-flight popped segments can be dropped); no test exercises join(timeout) with more than one process.

The production spawn-process path is never exercised — all tests pass produce_to_pipe and run flusher work as in-process threads — so spawn processes pickling the freshly-constructed per-shard SpansBuffer instances and sharing per-process mp_context.Values across process boundaries are never executed, meaning a pickling or cross-process Value regression would surface only in production.
`--flusher-processes=0` silently means maximum (one process per shard) because of the `or` fallback in `flusher.py:53-60`, the opposite of what an operator passing 0 would expect

A negative `flusher_processes` value produces an opaque `KeyError: 0` at startup: `range(-3)` yields an empty `process_to_shards_map`, then `i % num_processes == 0` indexes into the empty dict, with no validation or useful error

Inconsistent defaults across layers: the factory's default (`None`) means one process per shard while the CLI default (1) means legacy single-process, so programmatic construction of the factory (tests, future embedders — notably `test_basic`) silently gets a different process topology than production

Six parallel dicts keyed by `process_index` in `flusher.py:59-77` (`processes`, `buffers`, `process_to_shards_map`, `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, `process_restarts`) must be kept in sync across every lifecycle operation (create, restart, kill, join, health check) with nothing enforcing consistency; a single `FlusherProcess` record/class would make the invariants local

The injected `buffer` parameter is vestigial: it's used only for `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then discarded while `SpanFlusher` constructs its own `SpansBuffer`s internally; the signature should take `shards: list[int]` instead of a full `SpansBuffer`
`self.buffers` is fully derivable from `process_to_shards_map` and is redundant state

Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` (`flusher.py:~135-143`) is never called, and if ever wired up it would restart the process without killing the old one, causing a leaked/duplicate flusher; three near-identical method names (`_create_processes`, `_create_process_for_shards`, `_create_process_for_shard`) compound the confusion

Thread-mode restart leaks the old thread and runs duplicate flushers on the same shards: with `produce_to_pipe` set, the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard in `_ensure_processes_alive` means a hung thread is never stopped while `_create_process_for_shards` unconditionally starts a replacement over the same shards (`flusher.py:~245-250`)

`join()` skips `terminate()` (and waiting) for all remaining processes once the deadline expires: the `break` on `remaining_time <= 0` exits the loop before `process.terminate()` for the current and every subsequent process, leaving live processes behind on any non-final `join(timeout)` (`flusher.py:~331-346`)
`spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` metric semantics silently changed: one crash/hang now emits one `metrics.incr` per shard in the process's shard list (`flusher.py:~236-239`)
Comments describe a per-shard health model that doesn't exist, misleading readers about the actual per-process health tracking

New `shards` positional argument is prepended to the args tuple for both process targets, but only `SpanFlusher.main` (threading path) was re-signatured in the diff; the multiprocessing path target `_run_process` was never updated and previously received exactly six positional arguments, so production (spawn) flusher children will raise `TypeError: takes 7 positional arguments but 8 were given` at startup, exit immediately, and be restarted by `_ensure_processes_alive` until `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` is exceeded, causing `RuntimeError` → consumer restart → infinite crash loop → total outage of the span-buffer pipeline; every test sets `produce_to_pipe` (Thread path), so CI stays green while the production spawn path is unverified.

In the shutdown `join()` loop, when `remaining_time <= 0` the `break` exits before `process.terminate()` is reached, so the current process and every subsequent flusher process is never terminated or waited on; since `self.next_step.join(timeout)` consumes the same time budget first, hung flushers survive shutdown and orphaned processes accumulate during rebalance-driven strategy rebuilds, continuing to poll Redis and produce to Kafka alongside the replacement flusher.

The PR's core mechanism (flushing across multiple processes/shards) has zero functional test coverage: `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts wiring (process count, `max_processes`, shard-count totals), never submits a message or verifies that a segment in shard X is actually flushed by the process that owns shard X, and all other functional tests run with a single shard → single flusher, so per-process flush bugs keep CI green.

The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` in the test is a no-op because the same test starts with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, patching the time module globally; the synchronization described in the comment ('Give flusher threads time to process after drift change') does not exist, so the race it was presumably added to fix (flusher threads observing `current_drift.value = 9000` before `join()` sets `stopped`) remains unaddressed, along with the accompanying `django_db(transaction=True)` change made in the same 'make it pass' spirit.

Metrics tag key mismatch: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses tag key `shards` while sibling metrics in the same loop (`spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`, `flusher_unhealthy`) use `shard`, so the `wait_produce` series will not be selectable/joinable under the same tag key and dashboards/alerts filtering on `shard` will silently miss produce-wait latency.

`flusher_processes` programmatic default of `None` resolves via `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)` to one process per shard (N spawn children, each with its own Kafka producer), while the help text's 'Defaults to 1' only holds via the CLI's `default=1`; any construction path that misses the kwarg silently fans out to maximum.
`--flusher-processes 0` is swallowed by the `or` expression and silently means maximum fan-out rather than 'one/legacy' behavior.

Negative `flusher_processes` values are unvalidated: `min(-n, len(shards))` yields an empty `range(-n)` map, then `i % -n` raises a `KeyError` in `SpanFlusher.__init__`, causing the consumer to crash-loop at strategy creation instead of failing validation.

`max_processes` was inserted before `produce_to_pipe` in both `SpanFlusher.__init__` and the factory, so any positional caller passing the pipe as the 3rd argument now assigns a callable to `max_processes`.

Concurrent spawn stampede races the hang detector: all N flusher children are spawned simultaneously and each re-imports the full sentry app, while `process_healthy_since` is stamped at creation; on a loaded host, N concurrent heavy imports can exceed `spans.buffer.flusher.max-unhealthy-seconds`, causing healthy-but-still-starting processes to be killed → restart cascade → `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` → `RuntimeError` → consumer restart loop (the change multiplies the pre-existing single-process race's concurrent startup load by N).

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `SpanFlusher` run either as a `multiprocessing.Process` or as a `threading.Thread` when `produce_to_pipe` is set (see `_create_process_for_shards`: `make_process = threading.Thread`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, on a detected hang (`time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`) it restarts by calling `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` but only attempts to kill the worker if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. A hung `threading.Thread` is neither killed nor signaled to stop (the shared `self.stopped` flag remains false during normal operation), so the old thread can keep running while a new thread for the same `shards` is spawned. Because each restart creates a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` and the old thread still polls/flushes for the same shards, this can lead to concurrent duplicate flushing/producing for the same shards. The new code also avoids the old loud failure mode by skipping kill for threads, making the duplication risk silent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In flusher.py (~lines 45, 54), the unvalidated flusher_processes/max_processes value produces degenerate topologies with all self-protection disabled: --flusher-processes=0 is swallowed by the `or` and silently becomes one-process-per-shard, and a negative value yields min(-1, n) = -1 so range(-1) is empty and zero flusher processes are created. With empty processes/buffers, submit()'s guards are all vacuous (no backpressure rejection can ever fire and the Redis-memory check is skipped), so the consumer keeps buffering into Redis unboundedly while reporting healthy. click.Option(type=int) accepts these values.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `--flusher-processes` as a plain `click.Option(..., type=int)` with no validation, and `SpanFlusher.__init__` uses `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. This means `0` is silently treated as “unset” and becomes `len(assigned_shards)`, which is likely unintended. Worse, a negative value is truthy so `self.max_processes` stays negative, then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` can become `-1`. That makes `process_to_shards_map` empty (`range(self.num_processes)`), and the subsequent loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and then `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`, which will raise a `KeyError` (since the dict is empty). So the code can crash / behave incorrectly for user-supplied values introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In flusher.py (~line 202), the metric tag key mismatch fragments the flusher metrics: wait_produce is tagged {"shards": shard_tag} while produce and segment_size_bytes use {"shard": shard_tag}, so the same dimension lives under two tag keys and any dashboard/alert slicing spans.buffer.flusher.* by shard silently misses the wait_produce series.
matched_golden_ids: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate points out the same inconsistent metric tag key usage in the SpanFlusher flush loop: wait_produce uses "shards" while produce and segment_size_bytes use "shard", causing metric fragmentation and dashboards/alerts filtered by one tag to miss the other series.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py (~lines 62-65), the added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op: the test opens by monkeypatching time.sleep globally to a no-op lambda, so the intended wait to give flusher threads time to process after a drift change never happens and the test's actual stability rests on the flusher threads busy-spinning. The misleading comment could cause the test to break for the wrong reason if the monkeypatch is ever scoped.

In flusher.py join (~lines 334-345), the expired-deadline break abandons the remaining processes: waiting is sequential per process, so if the first (wedged) process consumes the whole deadline, the break skips both the wait and the terminate() for every remaining flusher process, losing the shutdown backstop for all but the first hung process (bounded impact since remaining processes observe the shared stopped flag and are daemons).

In factory.py:41 / flusher.py:47, the new flusher_processes/max_processes parameters were inserted mid-signature before produce_to_pipe: any positional caller passing the pipe callable as the next argument now binds it to flusher_processes, producing min(<callable>, len(...)) and a TypeError at construction, or for SpanFlusher a silently-None produce_to_pipe so produced payloads go nowhere. All in-diff callers use keywords, but out-of-diff positional callers are affected; the new params should be appended at the end instead.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` (factory.py) and `SpanFlusher.__init__` (flusher.py) gained a new optional parameter inserted *before* the existing `produce_to_pipe` parameter (`flusher_processes` / `max_processes` respectively). This changes positional-argument binding for any existing callers that passed `produce_to_pipe` positionally, potentially turning that callable into the new int parameter (or leaving `produce_to_pipe=None`). While all in-diff call sites use keywords, the signature change itself is real and could break out-of-diff positional callers; appending new optional params at the end would avoid that compatibility risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `flusher_processes` is unvalidated in flusher.py:51/60-66: a falsy `0` from `--flusher-processes 0` is silently swallowed by `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and becomes one process per assigned shard (a silent resource explosion of spawn-context interpreters, Redis pools, and Kafka producers contradicting the option's help text), while negative values pass through `min()` as negative, making `range(num_processes)` empty so `self.process_to_shards_map[0]` raises KeyError at :65-66 and crash-loops the consumer; needs `max(1, ...)` or explicit bounds validation.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit `max_processes=0` (possible via the new `--flusher-processes` click option, which has no bounds) as falsy and replaces it with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, defeating the configured limit and potentially spawning one process per shard. Also, negative values are not rejected: `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` can become negative, making `process_to_shards_map` empty (`range(self.num_processes)`), and then the shard-assignment loop does `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` with keys that don't exist (and/or `i % self.num_processes` behavior), causing runtime errors and consumer crash-looping. This is directly verifiable from the added logic in `flusher.py`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 Redis round-trips per submitted batch in `submit()` (flusher.py:269-270 and :300-302): new code loops over `self.buffers.values()` — one buffer per flusher process — issuing N sequential Redis round trips for the exact same total key set that a single all-shards buffer could have covered in one pipelined call, so per-batch ingestion latency grows linearly with process count whenever `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage < 1.0`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes SpanFlusher from a single `self.buffer` to multiple per-process `SpansBuffer` instances stored in `self.buffers` (created in `_create_process_for_shards`). In `submit()`, it now loops over `self.buffers.values()` to call `record_stored_segments()` and, when `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage < 1.0`, it loops again to aggregate `buffer.get_memory_info()` results. This makes the number of buffer operations per submit scale with the number of flusher processes. While the finding’s claim about Redis round-trips/pipelining depends on unseen `SpansBuffer` internals, the diff-grounded concern (per-submit work/latency increasing linearly with process count due to sequential per-buffer calls) is real and review-relevant, but it’s a performance/architecture regression rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hung flusher threads can't be killed but a replacement is spawned anyway (flusher.py:~246-256, `_ensure_processes_alive`): the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard means the threading (`produce_to_pipe`) mode never kills the unhealthy thread, yet `_create_process_for_shards()` immediately starts a second thread for the same shards — the hung thread leaks permanently, risks duplicate produce if it later un-hangs, and health monitoring only watches the replacement, making the zombie invisible; the old code at least failed loudly via `Thread.kill()` AttributeError.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, unhealthy workers are restarted via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` regardless of whether the existing worker is a `multiprocessing.Process` or a `threading.Thread`. However, the termination logic is guarded by `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`, so in `produce_to_pipe` mode (which uses `threading.Thread` in `_create_process_for_shards`) the unhealthy thread is never stopped. A new thread is started for the same shards and stored in `self.processes[process_index]`, leaving the old hung thread running but untracked (health monitoring only iterates `self.processes`). This can leak threads and can lead to duplicate flushing/produce if the old thread later resumes. The previous code would at least raise on `Thread.kill()` (not caught), but the new code silently replaces the thread without terminating it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric volume and cardinality multiplied by process count plus a tag-key inconsistency (flusher.py:~185-196, ~231-235, ~278-280): each of N processes emits `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `.wait_produce`, and `segment_size_bytes` per flush cycle tagged with a joined shard list that churns on every Kafka rebalance (unbounded distinct series), and `wait_produce` uses tag key "shards" while its siblings use "shard", splitting one logical metric into duplicate series.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds per-process metric tags based on a joined shard list: `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))`, then emits `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`. This will create distinct time series whenever shard groupings change (e.g., rebalances) and also increases metric emission volume with `num_processes`. Additionally, `wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (note plural key) while the related metrics use `"shard"`, splitting what should be one logical dimension into separate series.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `get_memory_info` summed across per-process buffers can double-count Redis services and skew the backpressure ratio (flusher.py:~300-303): if a Redis service hosts shards assigned to multiple processes under round-robin distribution, its stats are counted once per buffer instead of deduped as the old single all-shards buffer did, so the `used/available` ratio differs from the true cluster ratio and `max-memory-percentage` trips at the wrong point — over-rejecting messages or under-protecting Redis from OOM.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the memory check from a single `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` to aggregating `memory_infos` across multiple per-process `SpansBuffer` instances (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())` then summing `used`/`available`). That does create a concrete risk that the same underlying Redis service’s `ServiceMemory` stats could be included multiple times if `get_memory_info()` reports per-service (not per-shard) and multiple buffers touch the same service. The diff alone doesn’t show what `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` returns, so the skew/double-counting is not fully verifiable here, but the concern is specific and directly introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `join()` skips `terminate()` for all remaining processes once the shared deadline expires (flusher.py:~330-346): if the deadline expires while waiting on an early process, `break` exits the for-loop and every later child is never terminated, the first slow process consumes the entire timeout budget leaving the rest zero grace, and in the window before parent exit the un-terminated children keep polling Redis and can produce to Kafka after the pipeline has closed.
matched_golden_ids: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate describes that when the shared deadline expires, the code breaks out of the loop, which prevents terminate() from being called on remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown—exactly the golden concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new test wait is a no-op and the race it was added to fix remains (tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:~60-62): the added `time.sleep(0.1)` runs after `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` patches the global `time` module, so the test's own call is also a no-op and no time is actually yielded — if `step.join()` sets `stopped` before the flusher thread observes the drift change and produces, the segment is never flushed and assertions can fail intermittently; use a wait that bypasses the patch or restore it before sleeping.
matched_golden_ids: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes that `time.sleep` is monkeypatched to a no-op and therefore the subsequent `time.sleep(0.1)` in the test does not actually wait, leaving the race condition unfixed—same underlying problem as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spawn-mode entrypoint `SpanFlusher._main_process` was not updated for the new required `shards` parameter added to `main()`, so the multiprocessing target receives 7 positional args against a 6-parameter signature and crashes with a TypeError the moment each production flusher child process boots, causing a consumer crash loop after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS; CI won't catch it because tests pass `produce_to_pipe` and take the threading path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `SpanFlusher.main()` was updated to accept `shards: list[int]`, and `_create_process_for_shards` was also updated to pass `shards` as the first positional arg in `args=(shards, self.stopped, ...)` while binding `buffer` via `partial(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer)`. That yields a correct call signature. There is no `SpanFlusher._main_process` in the shown diff, and no evidence of a 7-vs-6 positional argument mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation on the `flusher_processes` CLI option: `--flusher-processes 0` silently spawns one process per shard (behavior inversion from `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)`), and negative values build an empty `process_to_shards_map` leading to a KeyError crash loop in `create_with_partitions`; needs `click.IntRange(min=1)` or an assert in `__init__`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `--flusher-processes` click option with `type=int` and no range validation. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `0` is treated as falsy and becomes `len(assigned_shards)` (inverting the intent of “0 processes” into “one per shard”). For negative values, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` can become negative, producing an empty `process_to_shards_map` (`range(self.num_processes)`), then `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` will raise `KeyError` because the dict is empty. This is a concrete crash scenario grounded in the new logic and warrants `IntRange(min=1)` or an explicit assert/guard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Long, high-cardinality shard-list tags (comma-joined list of all shards a process handles, e.g. '0,1,…,63' in the default config) are re-emitted on hot-path timers (`produce`, `segment_size_bytes`, `wait_produce`) every flush cycle, and the set of distinct tag values grows with every partition rebalance across the fleet, burdening the metrics pipeline.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the diff introduces `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` and then emits it on hot-path metrics every flush loop: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, and `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`. Since `shards` can be a long list per process and will vary across partition rebalances, this creates high-cardinality tag values and repeatedly emits them, which can burden the metrics pipeline. This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/architecture concern, not a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `flusher_unhealthy` now fans out per shard, so a single unhealthy process emits one increment per shard, making alert counts scale with shards-per-process (a single restart looks up to N× worse) and losing comparability with pre-PR dashboards.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, the diff changes `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", ...)` from a single increment per unhealthy flusher (previously one `self.process`) to incrementing once per shard handled by the unhealthy process: `for shard in shards: metrics.incr(... tags={..., "shard": shard})`. This will scale the counter by `len(shards)` for a single failure/hang of one process, which can inflate alert/dashboard counts and break comparability with pre-PR metrics behavior. This is a monitoring/observability semantics change rather than a correctness defect in processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag key: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": ...}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": ...}`, so timers describing the same flush cycle cannot be sliced/joined on a common dimension — almost certainly a typo.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metric tag keys in `SpanFlusher.main`: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use `shard`, while `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This won’t break runtime behavior but will fragment metrics dimensions and make related timers harder to correlate, consistent with a likely typo.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead helper `_create_process_for_shard` has no call sites and is a latent duplicate-flusher footgun: if ever wired up, it would start a second process for the shard group without killing the old one and without incrementing `process_restarts`, bypassing the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS safety and producing duplicate concurrent flushers/duplicate Kafka production; remove it or route it through the kill/restart path.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` a new helper `_create_process_for_shard` is added but has no call sites in the diff. Its implementation simply calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` without killing the existing process in `self.processes[process_index]` and without bumping `self.process_restarts[process_index]`, unlike the restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` which kills and increments before recreating. While this is not an active defect today (dead code), it is a diff-introduced, specific maintainability/footgun risk: if later wired up, it could spawn an additional flusher for the same shard group and bypass MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS tracking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `time.sleep(0.1)` added to `test_basic` is a no-op because the test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` globally, so the claimed 'give flusher threads time to process after drift change' synchronization doesn't exist and the test still relies on a race between the flusher thread reading `current_drift` and `step.join()`, remaining theoretically flaky.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the test sets `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` near the top. The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` later in the same test therefore calls the monkeypatched no-op and does not actually wait, despite the comment claiming it “Give flusher threads time to process”. This means the intended synchronization doesn’t exist and the test may still rely on timing/races around the flusher observing `current_drift` before `step.join()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Health check still only runs from `submit()`: `poll()` (invoked every arroyo loop iteration, even with no messages) only forwards to `next_step` and never invokes `_ensure_processes_alive()`, so an idle consumer never detects or restarts a dead flusher process until a message arrives, allowing Redis-buffered segments to age out past TTL and be lost.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher`, `poll()` still only delegates to `self.next_step.poll()` and does not call `_ensure_processes_alive()` (see `def poll(self) -> None:`). `_ensure_processes_alive()` is only invoked from `submit()` (`self._ensure_processes_alive()`), so if the consumer is idle (no submits) a dead/hung flusher process would not be detected/restarted by the regular arroyo loop calling `poll()`. That behavior is directly visible in the diff and can lead to prolonged non-flushing until the next message arrives.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new multiprocess test test_flusher_processes_limit verifies only internal wiring, never data flow: it submits no spans, never asserts messages or commits, and never inspects flusher.buffers[i] to confirm each per-process SpansBuffer was built from the correct shard subset, so a regression that passes the full shard list to every process (duplicate Kafka production of spans) or drops a shard from buffer construction (silent span loss) would pass undetected; the shard-total assertion (total_shards == 4) also cannot catch mis-assignment since a duplicated shard plus a dropped shard still sums to 4.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the new test only asserts internal attributes (`len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes`) and a weak shard-count sum (`total_shards == 4`) without exercising any end-to-end behavior (no `submit`, no produced `messages`, no `commits`). Given the new logic builds per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` in `_create_process_for_shards`, the test does not validate that each process/buffer got the correct shard subset (e.g., it wouldn’t detect duplicate shard assignment or a shard being dropped if the lengths still sum to 4). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The rewritten health-monitoring/restart logic in _ensure_processes_alive (per-process process_healthy_since dict, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS → RuntimeError, per-shard unhealthy metric fan-out, and the new isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)-guarded kill path) has zero test coverage; notably the isinstance guard is a behavior change — previously a thread-mode restart raised an uncaught AttributeError on Thread.kill(), whereas now the old (possibly hung) thread is silently left running while a new thread is started for the same shards — and nothing pins this new behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a worker is deemed unhealthy (`hang` via `process_healthy_since` or dead via `is_alive()`), the code restarts it by calling `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. However, the termination path is now guarded: `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`. In thread-mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None` → `make_process = threading.Thread`), the unhealthy thread is never stopped/terminated, yet a new thread is started for the same shard set. This can leave the old (possibly hung) thread running while duplicating work/resources, which is a concrete behavioral/regression risk introduced by the diff. The added tests only cover process-count/shard-mapping and do not exercise restart/health-monitoring behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The synchronization sleep added to test_basic is a no-op: the test monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op at its top, so the later time.sleep(0.1) intended to give flusher threads time to process after the drift change does literally nothing — either the author was ineffectively papering over a real race (drift change → flush ordering across threads) whose flake remains latent, or the line is dead code misleading future maintainers about how the test works.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the test immediately does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which patches `time.sleep` itself. The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` later in the same test therefore calls the patched no-op and does not actually wait, making the comment about “Give flusher threads time to process” misleading and not addressing any real race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The --flusher-processes click option is bare type=int with no bounds and the flusher performs no validation: flusher_processes=-1 yields max_processes = -1, an empty process_to_shards_map, and a KeyError in SpanFlusher.__init__ that crash-loops the consumer at startup; flusher_processes=0 silently falls through the 'or' to one-process-per-shard, contradicting the documented 'Defaults to 1' semantics; and no test covers 0, negative values, or the actual production default topology (1 process with many shards).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `--flusher-processes` click option with `type=int` and no validation, and the flusher code treats `max_processes` unsafely. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `0` is treated as falsy and replaced with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, contradicting the option’s documented semantics (default 1, but explicit 0 becomes “per-shard”). Worse, negative values are truthy: with `max_processes=-1`, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes `-1`, producing an empty `process_to_shards_map` (`range(-1)`), and then `process_index = i % self.num_processes` followed by `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` will raise `KeyError` because the map is empty. This is a concrete crash-at-startup path exposed by the new option.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric tag key mismatch in the new health metrics: wait_produce is tagged with tags={'shards': shard_tag} while produce and segment_size_bytes use tags={'shard': shard_tag}, so the wait-time series won't group with its sibling metrics in dashboards/alerts, and no test asserts the emitted tags, which is why the mismatch slipped through.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the new metrics tags are inconsistent: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This won’t break runtime behavior, but it will split time series and hinder grouping/alerts/dashboards for related metrics. The added/updated tests (`test_consumer.py`, `test_flusher.py`) don’t assert metric tag keys, so this kind of mismatch could slip through.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backpressure test coverage was weakened to an any() assertion (any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())) that only confirms at least one process noticed backpressure — a bug where some processes never record backpressure would still pass — and the new per-process gating semantics in submit() (raising MessageRejected when any single process exceeds the threshold, plus the per-process flusher.backpressure metric emission) have no coverage at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the backpressure assertion in `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py` from checking a single `flusher.backpressure_since.value` to `assert any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())`, which only verifies at least one per-process flag is set and would not catch a regression where other processes/shards never set backpressure. Separately, `SpanFlusher.submit()` now enforces backpressure by iterating all `process_backpressure_since` values and raising `MessageRejected` if any one exceeds the threshold, and `_ensure_processes_alive()` emits per-shard `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` metrics; the provided tests in the diff do not appear to exercise these new per-process gating/metric semantics. This is a concrete test coverage/strength issue, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Multi-process join(timeout) budget-sharing behavior changed and is untested: with multiple processes the first slow process can consume the entire timeout, and once remaining_time <= 0 the break skips both waiting and terminate() for all remaining processes (daemon=True masks the leak, but graceful drain is skipped and in-flight popped segments can be dropped); no test exercises join(timeout) with more than one process.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join`, the new multi-process loop can exit early when a shared `deadline` is exceeded: `if remaining_time <= 0: break` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py). That `break` skips the `while process.is_alive()` wait and also skips the `process.terminate()` block for all remaining flusher processes, leaving them running after `join(timeout)` returns. This behavior only exists because the diff changed from a single `self.process` to `self.processes` and added the deadline/break logic; previously there were no “remaining processes” to leak. The finding’s point that this multi-process timeout behavior is untested is also supported: added tests cover process count/shard distribution but do not call `join(timeout)` with multiple processes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The production spawn-process path is never exercised — all tests pass produce_to_pipe and run flusher work as in-process threads — so spawn processes pickling the freshly-constructed per-shard SpansBuffer instances and sharing per-process mp_context.Values across process boundaries are never executed, meaning a pickling or cross-process Value regression would surface only in production.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, the multiprocessing (spawn `Process`) path is only taken when `produce_to_pipe is None`; otherwise it runs `SpanFlusher.main` in a `threading.Thread` (`else: ... make_process = threading.Thread`). The updated/added tests shown (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`) both construct `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., produce_to_pipe=messages.append)`, which forces the thread path and avoids exercising the spawn-process pickling/IPC behavior (e.g., passing the newly created per-shard `SpansBuffer(shards)` and `mp_context.Value`s into a spawned process). That leaves a realistic gap in coverage for the production configuration without proving an immediate defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `--flusher-processes=0` silently means maximum (one process per shard) because of the `or` fallback in `flusher.py:53-60`, the opposite of what an operator passing 0 would expect

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means a CLI value of `--flusher-processes=0` (falsy) will be treated as “unset” and replaced with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, effectively enabling one process per shard. The new click option in `consumers/__init__.py` accepts any `int` and does not reject 0, so this surprising behavior is introduced/confirmed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A negative `flusher_processes` value produces an opaque `KeyError: 0` at startup: `range(-3)` yields an empty `process_to_shards_map`, then `i % num_processes == 0` indexes into the empty dict, with no validation or useful error

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `max_processes`/`flusher_processes` without validation. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will keep a negative value (truthy), then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes negative. This makes `process_to_shards_map = {i: [] for i in range(self.num_processes)}` empty (`range(-3)`), and the subsequent loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` (e.g., `0 % -3 == 0`) and then `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`, which raises `KeyError: 0`. This matches the finding: negative `flusher_processes` causes an opaque startup KeyError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent defaults across layers: the factory's default (`None`) means one process per shard while the CLI default (1) means legacy single-process, so programmatic construction of the factory (tests, future embedders — notably `test_basic`) silently gets a different process topology than production

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a real default mismatch: the CLI wiring in `ingest_transactions_options()` adds `--flusher-processes` with `default=1`, while `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` sets `flusher_processes: int | None = None` and passes it to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so `None` becomes `len(assigned_shards)` (effectively one process per shard), whereas the CLI default forces a single process. Programmatic users like `test_basic` construct the factory without `flusher_processes`, so they will get a different topology than production-by-default. This is a concrete, diff-grounded consistency/configuration concern, but not a directly verifiable correctness failure from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Six parallel dicts keyed by `process_index` in `flusher.py:59-77` (`processes`, `buffers`, `process_to_shards_map`, `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, `process_restarts`) must be kept in sync across every lifecycle operation (create, restart, kill, join, health check) with nothing enforcing consistency; a single `FlusherProcess` record/class would make the invariants local

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `SpanFlusher.__init__` introduces multiple parallel dicts keyed by `process_index` (`process_to_shards_map`, `processes`, `buffers`, `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`, `process_restarts`). Subsequent lifecycle code (_create_process_for_shards, _ensure_processes_alive, submit, join) relies on these structures staying consistent, but nothing in the diff enforces their invariants beyond developer discipline. This is a concrete maintainability/architecture risk introduced by the change rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The injected `buffer` parameter is vestigial: it's used only for `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then discarded while `SpanFlusher` constructs its own `SpansBuffer`s internally; the signature should take `shards: list[int]` instead of a full `SpansBuffer`

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the injected `buffer: SpansBuffer` is no longer stored (`self.buffer` removed) and is only used to derive shard info (`len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and iterating `for i, shard in enumerate(buffer.assigned_shards)`). Each worker then constructs its own `SpansBuffer(shards)` in `_create_process_for_shards`, so the original `buffer` instance is effectively discarded. This is a concrete API/architecture concern (unnecessary coupling / heavier parameter than needed), but it does not by itself show broken behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `self.buffers` is fully derivable from `process_to_shards_map` and is redundant state

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `self.buffers` is intentionally maintained alongside `process_to_shards_map`: `_create_process_for_shards` creates a `SpansBuffer(shards)` and stores it in `self.buffers[process_index]`, and `submit()` then iterates those buffer instances to call `record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info()`. While the shards list is derivable from `process_to_shards_map`, the corresponding `SpansBuffer` instances are not present unless constructed, and the code updates `self.buffers` on restarts. Calling this “redundant state” is a subjective refactor suggestion, not a concrete diff-grounded problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` (`flusher.py:~135-143`) is never called, and if ever wired up it would restart the process without killing the old one, causing a leaked/duplicate flusher; three near-identical method names (`_create_processes`, `_create_process_for_shards`, `_create_process_for_shard`) compound the confusion

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard` but nothing in the shown code calls it (the lifecycle uses `_create_processes()` on init and `_ensure_processes_alive()` for restarts). That makes it dead/unused code as of this PR. Also, if it were later wired up, it would call `_create_process_for_shards()` without first terminating the existing process for that `process_index`, unlike `_ensure_processes_alive()` which explicitly `kill()`s before restarting—so it could create duplicate/leaked workers. The presence of three similarly named helpers (`_create_processes`, `_create_process_for_shards`, `_create_process_for_shard`) is also directly visible and plausibly confusing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Thread-mode restart leaks the old thread and runs duplicate flushers on the same shards: with `produce_to_pipe` set, the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard in `_ensure_processes_alive` means a hung thread is never stopped while `_create_process_for_shards` unconditionally starts a replacement over the same shards (`flusher.py:~245-250`)

adjudication.rationale: In thread-mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread`, but `_ensure_processes_alive` only attempts to stop unhealthy workers via `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. For a hung thread, the code will still call `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` and start a new thread over the same shard list without any mechanism to stop the old thread (no per-thread stop flag; `self.stopped` is global and not set during restart). This can lead to multiple live flushers operating on the same shards and leaking the original thread.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `join()` skips `terminate()` (and waiting) for all remaining processes once the deadline expires: the `break` on `remaining_time <= 0` exits the loop before `process.terminate()` for the current and every subsequent process, leaving live processes behind on any non-final `join(timeout)` (`flusher.py:~331-346`)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()` the per-process loop does `if remaining_time <= 0: break` before reaching the `process.terminate()` call. That `break` exits the entire `for process_index, process in self.processes.items()` loop, so the current process (and any subsequent ones) will neither be waited on nor terminated when the timeout deadline is exceeded, potentially leaving live flusher processes behind on a non-final `join(timeout)` call (see added loop in `flusher.py` around the `remaining_time`/`break` and `process.terminate()` logic).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` metric semantics silently changed: one crash/hang now emits one `metrics.incr` per shard in the process's shard list (`flusher.py:~236-239`)

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `_ensure_processes_alive` now loops `for shard in shards:` and calls `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})`, so a single process crash/hang will emit multiple increments (one per shard assigned to that process). This is a real change from the prior single `metrics.incr(..., tags={"cause": cause})` behavior, affecting metric semantics/cardinality, but it’s not inherently a correctness defect in the runtime logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Comments describe a per-shard health model that doesn't exist, misleading readers about the actual per-process health tracking

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces per-process health tracking (`process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`) keyed by `process_index`, not per-shard health. However, comments imply a per-shard model, e.g. the class docstring says "Creates one process per shard" even though shards are distributed across `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` via `process_to_shards_map`, so multiple shards can share a process. Additionally, `_ensure_processes_alive` has a comment "Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy" but it only checks `time.time() - process_healthy_since[...]`, i.e., process-level liveness/health, not shard-level. This is misleading documentation but not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New `shards` positional argument is prepended to the args tuple for both process targets, but only `SpanFlusher.main` (threading path) was re-signatured in the diff; the multiprocessing path target `_run_process` was never updated and previously received exactly six positional arguments, so production (spawn) flusher children will raise `TypeError: takes 7 positional arguments but 8 were given` at startup, exit immediately, and be restarted by `_ensure_processes_alive` until `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` is exceeded, causing `RuntimeError` → consumer restart → infinite crash loop → total outage of the span-buffer pipeline; every test sets `produce_to_pipe` (Thread path), so CI stays green while the production spawn path is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly prepends `shards` into the `args=(shards, ...)` tuple for *both* targets in `_create_process_for_shards`. The threading target is `partial(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer)` and `SpanFlusher.main(...)` was re-signatured to accept `shards: list[int]`, so that path is consistent. The multiprocessing target remains `partial(SpanFlusher._run_process, shard_buffer)`, but `_run_process`’s signature is not shown/changed in this diff, so the claimed concrete `TypeError` in production cannot be verified from the diff alone. What *is* verifiable is that tests all set `produce_to_pipe=...`, forcing the threading path, so the spawn/multiprocessing path is not exercised in CI despite nontrivial argument/launch changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the shutdown `join()` loop, when `remaining_time <= 0` the `break` exits before `process.terminate()` is reached, so the current process and every subsequent flusher process is never terminated or waited on; since `self.next_step.join(timeout)` consumes the same time budget first, hung flushers survive shutdown and orphaned processes accumulate during rebalance-driven strategy rebuilds, continuing to poll Redis and produce to Kafka alongside the replacement flusher.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the per-process loop checks `remaining_time = deadline - time.time()` and if `remaining_time <= 0` executes `break` *before* the `while process.is_alive()` wait and before the `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()` call. Since `self.next_step.join(timeout)` runs first and can consume the whole time budget, it’s possible to hit `remaining_time <= 0` on the first flusher process and exit without terminating (or waiting on) any flusher processes. The diff shows no later cleanup after the loop, so multiprocessing flushers can survive shutdown when time is exhausted (especially if hung), matching the finding’s core concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The PR's core mechanism (flushing across multiple processes/shards) has zero functional test coverage: `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts wiring (process count, `max_processes`, shard-count totals), never submits a message or verifies that a segment in shard X is actually flushed by the process that owns shard X, and all other functional tests run with a single shard → single flusher, so per-process flush bugs keep CI green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior in `SpanFlusher`: splitting `buffer.assigned_shards` across multiple worker processes/threads (`process_to_shards_map`), creating per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)`, and handling per-process health/backpressure tracking and restarts. The newly added `test_flusher_processes_limit` only validates configuration/wiring (`len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and that shard IDs are assigned in the map) and never drives the system by submitting messages/segments and asserting they are flushed/produced correctly per shard/process. From the diff, there is no test that exercises the correctness of the new multi-process shard distribution and flushing behavior (beyond construction-time assertions), which is a concrete coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, but not itself a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` in the test is a no-op because the same test starts with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, patching the time module globally; the synchronization described in the comment ('Give flusher threads time to process after drift change') does not exist, so the race it was presumably added to fix (flusher threads observing `current_drift.value = 9000` before `join()` sets `stopped`) remains unaddressed, along with the accompanying `django_db(transaction=True)` change made in the same 'make it pass' spirit.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the test starts with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which patches `time.sleep` on the imported `time` module. The newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` later in the same test therefore calls the patched no-op function and does not actually wait, making the comment "Give flusher threads time to process" inaccurate and providing no real synchronization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metrics tag key mismatch: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses tag key `shards` while sibling metrics in the same loop (`spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`, `flusher_unhealthy`) use `shard`, so the `wait_produce` series will not be selectable/joinable under the same tag key and dashboards/alerts filtering on `shard` will silently miss produce-wait latency.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent metrics tag keys: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use `shard`, while `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This will split the time series across different tag keys and make filtering/joining on `shard` miss `wait_produce` data. It’s a concrete observability issue introduced by the change, but not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `flusher_processes` programmatic default of `None` resolves via `max_processes or len(assigned_shards)` to one process per shard (N spawn children, each with its own Kafka producer), while the help text's 'Defaults to 1' only holds via the CLI's `default=1`; any construction path that misses the kwarg silently fans out to maximum.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a mismatch in defaults: CLI adds `--flusher-processes` with `default=1` and help text “Defaults to 1.”, but programmatic construction defaults `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.flusher_processes` to `None` (factory.py) and passes it through to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` makes `None` resolve to `len(assigned_shards)`, i.e., one process per shard. This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency/documentation/behavior surprise for non-CLI call paths, but it’s not provably a correctness defect without an explicit spec that the programmatic default must also be 1.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `--flusher-processes 0` is swallowed by the `or` expression and silently means maximum fan-out rather than 'one/legacy' behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` as falsy, so providing `--flusher-processes 0` (passed as `max_processes=0`) will be converted to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, i.e. maximum fan-out. The click option has `type=int` with no lower-bound validation, so `0` is a plausible input and this would silently change behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Negative `flusher_processes` values are unvalidated: `min(-n, len(shards))` yields an empty `range(-n)` map, then `i % -n` raises a `KeyError` in `SpanFlusher.__init__`, causing the consumer to crash-loop at strategy creation instead of failing validation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new CLI option `--flusher-processes` with `type=int` and no validation (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py), plumbs it through `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)` (factory.py). In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will keep a negative value (truthy), then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes negative. This leads to `process_to_shards_map = {i: [] for i in range(self.num_processes)}` being empty (negative range) and the subsequent `process_index = i % self.num_processes` / `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` causing a KeyError during initialization. So a negative input can crash strategy creation, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `max_processes` was inserted before `produce_to_pipe` in both `SpanFlusher.__init__` and the factory, so any positional caller passing the pipe as the 3rd argument now assigns a callable to `max_processes`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the positional parameter order by inserting `max_processes` before `produce_to_pipe` in `SpanFlusher.__init__` (and similarly inserts `flusher_processes` before `produce_to_pipe` in `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__`). This means any existing callers that passed `produce_to_pipe` positionally would now accidentally pass that callable into the new integer parameter. In this diff, the factory calls `SpanFlusher` using keyword arguments, so the factory itself is not broken here, but the API change is real and could break other positional call sites (not shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrent spawn stampede races the hang detector: all N flusher children are spawned simultaneously and each re-imports the full sentry app, while `process_healthy_since` is stamped at creation; on a loaded host, N concurrent heavy imports can exceed `spans.buffer.flusher.max-unhealthy-seconds`, causing healthy-but-still-starting processes to be killed → restart cascade → `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` → `RuntimeError` → consumer restart loop (the change multiplies the pre-existing single-process race's concurrent startup load by N).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple spawned flusher processes started in a tight loop (`_create_processes` → `_create_process_for_shards`), while the hang detector in `_ensure_processes_alive` uses `process_healthy_since[process_index].value` stamped at process creation (`_create_process_for_shards` sets it to `int(time.time())` before `process.start()`). That value is only updated inside `SpanFlusher.main` after the child finishes spawning/importing and enters its loop (`healthy_since.value = system_now`). If startup (spawn + imports) takes longer than `spans.buffer.flusher.max-unhealthy-seconds`, the parent will treat the process as “hang” and kill/restart it, potentially repeating until `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` and raising `RuntimeError`, restarting the consumer. Spawning N processes concurrently increases the likelihood vs the prior single-process design.
